verdict.rationale: Jev natively returns typed answers in three formats: Choice (the selected option plus per-option probabilities), Score (a level plus per-level probabilities) and Noul (a yes/no probability). Its SDKs expose these as typed questions and answers that code consumes directly, which satisfies the 'natively typed answer format' half of the story. That typed surface is limited to these three decision primitives, and there is no documented arbitrary JSON-schema-constrained output; JSON structure is accepted on inputs (instructions, options, levels, criteria), not as an output schema. missing for 10: arbitrary JSON-schema-constrained response output beyond Choice/Score/Noul, documented structured extraction/generation of free-form typed objects, and independent hands-on corroboration of the typed-answer parsing workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get typed, structured outputs — JSON-schema-constrained responses or a natively typed answer format — so my code consumes model output without fragile parsing
